Position, Distance and Displacement: Position is the location of an object on a number line relative to a chosen origin, with a sign for direction. Distance is the total path length, a scalar that is never negative. Displacement is the change in position, x_final minus x_initial, and is a vector whose sign shows direction. Distance is always at least as large as the size of the displacement, and the two are equal only for straight motion without reversing. A round trip has zero displacement but nonzero distance.
Average Speed and Velocity: Average speed is total distance divided by total time and is a scalar. Average velocity is displacement divided by time, v = change in x over change in t, and is a vector with a sign for direction. Both are measured in m/s, and km/h is converted by dividing by 3.6. A round trip has zero average velocity. With constant velocity the position is x = x0 + vt. Average speed over a multi-part trip must use total distance over total time, not an average of the speeds.
Acceleration and Changing Velocity: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, a = (v - v0) / t, measured in m/s^2. It is a vector, so speeding up, slowing down and changing direction are all acceleration. If velocity and acceleration point the same way the object speeds up; if opposite, it slows down. Zero velocity does not imply zero acceleration, as at the top of a thrown ball. Always subtract final minus initial velocity to keep the sign correct.
Equations of Motion with Constant Accele: For constant acceleration four equations connect the variables: v = v0 + at, d = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2, v^2 = v0^2 + 2ad, and d = ((v0 + v)/2) t. Choose the one that contains the unknown and omits the quantity you do not know, and keep signs consistent, so braking has negative acceleration. Stopping distance grows with the square of the initial speed. The equations do not apply after the object stops or when acceleration changes.
Free Fall and Motion Graphs: In free fall, ignoring air resistance, every object accelerates at g = 9.8 m/s^2 downward regardless of mass, including while rising and at the top of its path where v = 0. From rest, v = gt and d = (1/2) g t^2. On a position-time graph the slope is velocity. On a velocity-time graph the slope is acceleration and the area under the line is displacement. A straight position-time line means constant velocity.
